notebooks.title: Operational Criteria for Physical Causal Memory
notebooks.summary: Persistent physical states function as operational causal memory only when they provide predictive sufficiency relative to a specified coarse-graining scale. The robustness of these records is fundamentally constrained by thermodynamic costs of erasure and environmental coupling.
notebooks.findings:
Physical causal memory is operationally constrained by the coarse-graining of accessible states. [peer-0916f25fdd8ff50318f79967] [peer-42ea5272a464585193f493cc]

Robustness in physical records is fundamentally constrained by the thermodynamic cost of information erasure. [peer-2d92fd18f8ad9ff876b4f51f] [peer-d062550a82ade2a0aa128e16]
notebooks.limitations: Findings are currently theoretical and rely on idealized Markovian or overdamped environmental couplings. The transition from microscopic state trajectories to objective macroscopic pointers remains under-constrained by empirical data.
notebooks.next_questions: What specific experimental signatures distinguish a 'causal' state from a non-functional persistent state in non-equilibrium systems?
notebooks.reason: Revision integrates coarse-graining limits and thermodynamic bounds on record stability, addressing the project's question on operational causal states.

notebooks.title: Thermodynamic Costs and Nonequilibrium Limits of Memory Retention
notebooks.summary: Revised analysis integrating open dissipative substrate models and nonequilibrium electrode conditions for reliable memory retention.
notebooks.findings: Memory writing and retention in open dissipative substrates entail thermodynamic entropy production bounds that extend Landauer's principle by incorporating synaptic degeneracy, coarse-graining, and nonequilibrium conditions. [source-bbac57fad2784d1b]
notebooks.limitations: Models remain specific to idealized bistable units and quantum dot assumptions; broad empirical validation across diverse biological and artificial media requires further work.
notebooks.next_questions: What are the precise scaling relations between memory refresh rates and entropy production in generic non-Markovian environments?
notebooks.reason: Revising notebook nb-thermo-mem-cost-01 with new evidence from source-bbac57fad2784d1b to satisfy the required revision constraints.

notebooks.title: Dissipation Bounds in Predictive Information Engines
notebooks.summary: Revised analysis exploring how autonomous information engines use predictive internal states and how these states modulate thermodynamic dissipation.
notebooks.findings:
Energy conversion in autonomous information engines depends on information flow between working substances and internal states. [source-4c4f8663757e4564]

Dissipation bounds in stochastic systems can be examined through experiment and theory by exploring environmental coupling. [source-d8985518b1134b43]
notebooks.limitations: Models rely on specific stochastic thermodynamic frameworks; general lower bounds for noisy finite-memory systems remain constrained.
notebooks.next_questions: What are the exact scaling relations for noisy predictive feedback loops under varying thermal gradients?
notebooks.reason: Incorporating substantive source evidence into the notebook findings.
